messages:
maya: quick heads-up — after landing PR #482 the long-seq perf job shows a noticeable regression. p50 ~+18%, p99 ~+35%. :eyes:

ajay: ugh. did we change kernel selection or batching heuristics in that PR? any nsys traces?

maya: i ran a quick nsys comparison (before vs after) and uploaded the qdrep/qdstr files: https://perf.redwood.example/runs/17678-flame-before.qdrep and https://perf.redwood.example/runs/17678-flame-after.qdrep

maya: tl;dr from the flame: 'kernel_kv_read' went from ~12% GPU time to ~38%, and memcpy H2D spikes where it previously was ~4% now ~22%. nvtx spans around kv lookup are much wider.

chris: that smells like a KV cache eviction / eviction-induced memcpy storm. PR #482 touched the kernel-chooser policy (fallback to matmul_alt for medium seqs) and also adjusted the batcher headroom.

ajay: can you paste the nsys stats snippet? even top-10 kernels with % would help.

maya: sure — raw excerpt from nsys stats on the "after" run:
```
CUDA kernels by GPU time:
1 kernel_kv_read                 38.1%   4300 ms
2 memcpy_h2d                    22.3%   2520 ms
3 matmul_alt_kernel              12.4%   1400 ms
4 softmax_fwd                    8.7%    980 ms
...
```

maya: before run had memcpy_h2d 4.2% and kernel_kv_read 11.8%.

chris: interesting — kernel_kv_read jump could be due to more cache misses (evictions) or a different launch config that serializes reads. Did the PR change the KV prefetch / caching policy?

maya: PR changed the prefetch window from 64->32 for medium sequences (intended to reduce memory pressure). looks like it increased read thrashing.

ajay: ok plan: reproduce locally with the bench script 'bench/long_seq.sh' and capture nsys on both HEAD~1 and HEAD. we should bisect if needed.

chris: bisect steps:
```
git checkout main
git bisect start --bad HEAD --good HEAD~20
# run bench/long_seq.sh (nsys profile)
# mark good/bad according to p50 threshold
git bisect good|bad
```
I'll drop a small helper that automates the run and extracts p50 from logs.

perf-bot: deploy: release/482 promoted to dedicated at 2025-03-11T09:12Z by ci/deploy (release id: r482) :rocket:

maya: thanks. i'm attaching the benchmark command i used:
```
NSYS_OPTS="--trace=nvtx,cuda,osrt" nsys profile -o after_run ./bench/long_seq.sh --variant=dedicated --iters=20
nsys stats after_run.qdrep --report=summary
```

ajay: capture both qdrep and perfetto trace (`--trace=osrt,perfetto`) so we can inspect host<->gpu timeline. perfetto helps see memcpy bursts and thread scheduling.

maya: uploaded perfetto slice: https://perf.redwood.example/trace/17678-perfetto-after.html — shows repeated memcpy H2D bursts aligned with worker thread wakeups.

chris: that aligns with a batching / scheduler hiccup. if batcher headroom got smaller, more frequent, smaller batches could trigger more synchronous memory copies.

ajay: can we try toggling the kernel chooser back to old heuristic locally (env var KERNEL_CHOOSER=legacy) and see perf?

maya: tried that — with KERNEL_CHOOSER=legacy the after-run drops memcpy to ~6% and kernel_kv_read to ~13%, overall p50 returns to baseline.

chris: solid repro then. likely culprit = kernel chooser change interacting with prefetch window tweak. let's bisect to the exact commit for PR #482. maya — can you run `git bisect` with my helper and push the resulting good/bad marker?

maya: starting now. helper is at tools/perf_bisect.py — it runs bench, collects qdrep, parses p50. i'll iterate and report back.

[~20m later]

maya: git bisect pointed to commit b3a1f2d as first bad. commit message: "adaptive-kchooser: prefer matmul_alt for medium seqs + prefetch window 32".

ajay: ok that's the merge. next: create a minimal reproducer that toggles only the kchooser flag vs only the prefetch change to see which sub-change triggers the memcpy spike.

chris: also collect a short nvprof run (or cupti counters) to check memory copy path (pinned vs pageable) — if prefetch removed pinning or changed buffer lifetimes we could be forcing pageable copies which are slower/serialized.

maya: nvprof snippet shows host->device copy type changed to pageable for many transfers in the after run. before copies were pinned. excerpt:
```
HostToDevice memcpy: pageable 23.1% (after) vs pinned 3.9% (before)
```

ajay: that nails it — prefetch window shrink probably changed allocation path. either prefetcher stopped using a pinned staging buffer pool or eviction policy freed pinned buffers early.

chris: good catch. mitigation: revert prefetch window change and add an explicit pinned staging pool allocation in the prefetcher. also add a perf test that asserts pinned-copy ratio > 90% for long_seq.

maya: will open PR to revert + add pinned pool + test. assigning to @ajay for follow-up on kernel chooser behavior (we may still want that optimization but need safe integration).

perf-bot: note: creating ticket INF-1283 with linked traces and bisect result.

ajay: i'll take INF-1283 and start the pinned-pool PR. thanks for the reproducible traces, maya. :thumbsup:

chris: add an e2e guard in CI that runs bench/long_seq on a small scale with nsys sampling to detect future memcpy regressions. we should fail merge if memcpy_h2d % > 10% baseline.

maya: agreed. I'll add the CI job and upload the before/after qdrep artifacts to the run for easier review.

maya: tl;dr — root cause = prefetch window change leading to pageable host copies and KV read churn; bisect -> commit b3a1f2d; immediate action: revert prefetch tweak, implement pinned staging pool, add perf CI guard.

chris: thanks all. next status in #eng-runtime when PRs are up.
